root_idea.summary: The root centers on whiteness, especially whiteness as a color, and extends to things named or understood through resemblance to an egg or through the protection and enclosure associated with it.
root_idea.development: The basic color term gives rise to the egg and helmet senses, then to figurative uses for protected territory, a central collective body, an established situation, and several idioms based on whiteness or egg-like form.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Form IX is a distinct Quran-attested verbal lexeme; its public citation form is the third-person masculine perfect.
This group represents the adjective أَبْيَضُ and its feminine and plural inflections.
This is the distinct noun بَيْضٌ, ‘eggs,’ in the Quranic simile.

senses.definition: To become white; to turn white.
senses.usage_conditions: An intransitive change of color. In the Quran it is used of faces and, in another passage, of eyes; the difference is contextual rather than a separate lexical meaning.

senses.definition: Of faces, to become radiant with joy or gladness.
senses.usage_conditions: A figurative use in which whitening of the face expresses happiness and well-being, in contrast with blackening as an expression of grief or punishment.

quranic_forms.public_pos_label: Adjective · with feminine and plural forms

senses.definition: White; having the color or visible quality of whiteness.
senses.usage_conditions: The group includes أَبْيَضُ, its feminine بَيْضَاءُ, and the plural بِيضٌ. The Quranic uses include a white thread or streak, a shining hand, white mountain streaks, and a white drink.
The ordinary noun for eggs, named for their whiteness.

senses.definition: In a simile, protected or concealed women likened to eggs.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic expression presents women as resembling eggs kept hidden and protected; this is a conventional metonymic or simile-based use rather than a claim that the referents are literally eggs.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To surpass someone in whiteness.
Of a bird, to lay an egg or eggs.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of an ostrich, hen, bird, or similar egg-laying creature.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of clouds, to rain.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To remain, stay, or become established in a place.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The expression evokes a bird remaining where it lays its eggs.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of the earth, to produce truffles or vegetation; or to turn yellow, shed its produce, and dry up.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Figurative applications of the egg-producing image; the alternatives are lexically reported variants.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For heat to become vehement or intense.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To whiten something, make it white, bleach it, whitewash it, or tin it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The causative Form II use is the counterpart of making something black.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make someone joyful or cheerful; figuratively, to clear or vindicate the person’s character.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An idiomatic causative use of whitening the face.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To produce a fair copy or clean transcript from a rough draft.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Reported as probably post-classical.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To fill a vessel or skin with water or milk.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative Form II use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To empty a vessel.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reported contrary meaning of the same Form II verb.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To contend with someone for superiority in whiteness.
To act openly or frankly with someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative association with the whiteness or daylight of day.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a man or woman, to beget or bear white children.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized reproductive use, distinct from becoming white.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To put an iron helmet upon oneself.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The helmet is called بَيْضَةٌ because of its egg-like shape.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To enter into a people’s territory, stronghold, or principal quarter.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The object is بَيْضَةٌ in its territorial or collective sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To exterminate or extirpate a people; to smite their collective body and seize what belongs to them by force.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The associated territory or central body may thereby be given up to plunder.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of herbage or pasture, to become pale or white and dry up.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized use of Form IX, distinct from the Quranic color-change and face expressions.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An egg, especially that of an ostrich or other bird.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The word is also used for the egg of anything described as having an egg-like form.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For what was hidden in a people’s affair or case to become apparent.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative expression based on a young bird emerging from an egg.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An ostrich egg abandoned in the open; figuratively, an isolated, abject, obscure, or unsupported person, or conversely a protected, pre-eminent, unrivalled chief.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The idiom has opposed blame and praise uses, depending on whether the abandoned egg or the protected egg is intended.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An iron helmet.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A noun of resemblance to an ostrich egg.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A testicle.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative anatomical use based on form and whiteness; plural بِيضَانٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The bulb of the saffron plant.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Named for its egg-like shape.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A tuber.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reported figurative use based on shape.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A large white grape of al-Ṭāʾif.
The core of a boil.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Named for its egg-like appearance.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The fat of a camel’s hump.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative use based on resemblance to an egg.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A white truffle, or truffles.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An additional regional or figurative use of the expression.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A container, encompassing territory, or central collective body; hence the territory, governing center, or assembled community of Islam or of a people.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: In expressions such as بَيْضَةُ الإِسْلَامِ and بَيْضَةُ القَوْمِ, the word can denote the protected domain, central quarter, governing seat, or collective body.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A secluded damsel or woman protected within a curtained chamber.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The woman is likened to an egg concealed and protected beneath a wing or covering.

other_classical_meanings.definition: White, smooth, barren, or uncultivated land.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The land is characterized by the absence of vegetation; this is a figurative land term, not the ordinary color adjective.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The whiteness or light of day; daylight.
The most vehement heat of summer or the hottest period of summer.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Also used of the main or intensely hot part of summer.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Whiteness, the opposite of blackness, in an animal, plant, water, or other thing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The related form بَيَاضَةٌ is used especially for whiteness of the eye.

other_classical_meanings.definition: White clothing or garments.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An elliptical use for something possessing whiteness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Milk.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative use based on its whiteness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The white of an egg.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized partitive use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Land without cultivation, population, or similar habitation.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative use of whiteness for bare or unproductive land.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The part of the skin on which there is no hair.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized anatomical use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person or individual.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative use parallel to سَوَادٌ for a person or personal presence.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A hen that lays many eggs; by extension, an oviparous creature.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The form may also be used more generally for an egg-laying animal.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A bird or similar creature that lays an egg or eggs; by extension, one credited with begetting eggs.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term may be applied figuratively to a cock or crow as well as to a hen or bird.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A bleacher of clothes.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A professional noun, not the ordinary active participle of بَيَّضَ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An egg seller.
Of a person, white or fair in complexion; of the face, clear of freckles or unsightly blackness.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Classical personal description; the source also records differing preferences for other color terms in descriptions of complexion.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a person, pure, faultless, unsullied in honor, noble, or generous.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative moral and social use, distinct from the Quranic color adjective.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An army or military detachment whose iron arms or armor show white.
A blank sheet or piece of paper.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A substantivized use of the feminine adjective.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A sword.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Named for the whiteness or brightness of its blade.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Silver.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Named for its whiteness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The saliva of the mouth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reported substantival use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A certain star at the margin of the Milky Way.
The sun.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative name based on whiteness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Waste, uncultivated, or uninhabited land.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative land term, opposed to the dark or cultivated land.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Wheat.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A substantival use based on its pale color.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Fresh grain of the kind called سُلْت.
A kind of white wood, identified with الحَوَرُ.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Named for its whiteness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The cooking pot.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A substantival lexical use; أُمُّ بَيْضَاءُ is also reported.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A snare for catching game.
The ‘two whites’: a conventional pair such as milk and water, bread and water, wheat and water, or fat and milk.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The exact pair varies among reported usages.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A man’s fat and youthfulness.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: In ذَهَبَ أَبْيَضَاهُ, these qualities are said to have departed.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Two days, or according to another report, two months.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in the temporal expression مَا رَأَيْتُهُ مُذْ أَبْيَضَانِ; the sources disagree over the interval.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The days of the bright full-moon nights, conventionally the thirteenth, fourteenth, and fifteenth days of the lunar month.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A variant count is reported, but the three-day period is identified as the stronger explanation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A year of scarcity of herbage, intermediate between the kinds called شَهْبَاء and حَمْرَاء.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized pastoral expression.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Clear, explained, or fully expounded speech.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative use of whiteness for clarity.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Neither a bad word nor a good word; neither a negative nor an affirmative reply.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A fixed contrastive expression.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A manifesting or demonstrated argument, plea, allegation, or proof.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative expression of evident force or clarity.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An unsolicited favor or benefit for which its recipient is not reproached.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A distinct figurative use of the same expression.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Sudden death, especially death not preceded by an illness that alters the complexion.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: It may also be explained as death without the usual opportunity for repentance, prayer for forgiveness, and completion of duties; it is opposed to red death, slaughter.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A calamity or misfortune.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Reported as a euphemistic or auspiciously worded term.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A place where eggs are laid.
A woman who bears white children.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized feminine noun; مُوضِحَةٌ is reported as more common for this meaning.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A fair copy or clean transcript made from a rough draft.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Reported as probably post-classical.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A man wearing white clothing.
A sect known as the ‘White-clad’ sect.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The name refers to its white clothing, in contrast to the black-clad opposing faction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For a woman’s hand to swell in a shape resembling an egg.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative anatomical use reported in Quran-focused lexical discussion.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Pointer to the main بَيْضَةٌ entry.

cautions: The QAC adjective group combines masculine, feminine, and plural inflections under أَبْيَضُ, while the noun بَيْضٌ in 37:49 is displayed separately.

Lane's printed Quran reference associated with the egg/woman simile uses historical citation notation; the modern example location 37:49 is used because that location is independently supplied by QAC.
